content: This document provides a chronological list of significant epidemics throughout history: Between 165 and 180 CE, the Antonine Plague occurred, which is believed to have been caused by smallpox. In 541 CE, the Plague of Justinian emerged, marking one of the earliest recorded pandemics. During the 1300s, the Black Death devastated populations across Europe, Asia, and North Africa. From 1501 to 1587, typhus outbreaks were widespread. In 1732–1733, an influenza epidemic was recorded. Another influenza outbreak occurred in 1775–1776. Between 1816 and 1826, the first cholera pandemic took place. The second cholera pandemic spanned from 1829 to 1851. An influenza epidemic occurred in 1847–1848. The third cholera pandemic lasted from 1852 to 1860. From 1855 to the 1950s, the Third Pandemic of bubonic plague persisted, originating in China and spreading globally. An influenza outbreak was recorded between 1857 and 1859. The fourth cholera pandemic occurred from 1863 to 1875. An influenza epidemic took place between 1889 and 1892. The fifth cholera pandemic spanned from 1899 to 1923. The Spanish flu pandemic, caused by an avian influenza virus, occurred between 1918 and 1920. This pandemic resulted in more hospitalizations during World War I than injuries caused by combat.
